stem:
Kartik starts with lemon juice that turns blue litmus solution red. He adds lime water a little at a time until the mixture is neither acidic nor basic, and the tube feels slightly warm.

Which explanation is best?

options.text: Enough base mixed with the acid produced a neutral effect, with salt, water, and heat as the usual companions of that change.
One drop of lime water is enough to neutralise any amount of lemon juice.
Any glass of plain water that tests neutral must have been made by mixing an acid and a base.
At the neutral point the blue-litmus mixture must become colourless.

teacher.key_rationale: Neutralisation needs sufficient opposite natures mixed together. One drop for any amount omits quantity; assuming every neutral water came from acid+base reverses the inference; requiring colourlessness captures a surface colour expectation.
